data.title: Oral argument
data.text:
(1) Unless otherwise directed, (a) all appeals will be set down on the Civil Appeal Hearing List for an oral hearing, and (b) the appeal and any cross appeal will be argued at the same time.
(2) On agreement of all parties or on the direction of a single appeal judge, , the Court of Appeal may hear and decide an appeal without oral argument.
(3) The Court of Appeal may proceed with the hearing of an appeal when scheduled, even if (a) a party does not appear at the scheduled time, or (b) any party has failed to file its factum.
(4) Unless the panel otherwise permits, oral argument must not exceed 45 minutes for each separately represented party in the appeal, with any consolidated appeals to be treated as one appeal.
(5) Repealed AR 194/2020 s8.

data.title: Scheduling standard appeals
data.text:
(1) No later than 20 days after the deadline for the filing of the last factum in a standard appeal, (a) the parties must contact the Registrar to schedule the oral hearing, and (2) Any standard appeal that has not been scheduled for an oral hearing and placed on the Civil Appeal Hearing List before (a) the earlier of (i) 2 months after the deadline for the filing of the last factum in the appeal, and (ii) 9 months after the filing of the notice of appeal, or (b) any deadline stipulated by a case management officer or a single appeal judge must be referred to a case management officer for further direction.

data.title: Scheduling fast track appeals
data.text:
(1) The Registrar must schedule fast track appeals in accordance with these rules.
(2) The Registrar must place on the Civil Appeal Hearing List (a) any fast track appeal for which the Appeal Record and the appellant’s factum and Extracts of Key Evidence have been filed 20 or more days before the opening of the sittings, and (b) any fast track appeal that a case management officer directs to be scheduled for hearing.
(3) Despite subrule (2), the parties may, no less than 20 days before the opening of the sittings, consent to an adjournment of the oral hearing of a fast track appeal to no later than the next sitting of the Court, provided that the appeal has not previously been adjourned more than once.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021); Alta.*

data.title: Rescheduling appeals
data.text:
(1) Subject to Rule 14.34(3) [Scheduling fast track appeals], a scheduled oral hearing may not be adjourned or rescheduled unless the appeal has been discontinued or settled or a case management officer permits the hearing to be adjourned or rescheduled.
(2) A case management officer may at any time set down or reschedule an appeal, or place any appeal on or remove any appeal from the Civil Appeal Hearing List.

data.title: Single appeal judges
data.text:
(1) Unless an enactment or these rules otherwise require, a single appeal judge may hear and decide any application incidental to an appeal, including those that could have been decided by a case management officer.
(2) For greater certainty, a single appeal judge may (a) grant permission to appeal, unless an enactment requires that an application for permission to appeal must be heard by a panel of the Court of Appeal, (b) declare an appeal to be struck, dismissed or abandoned for failure to comply with a mandatory rule, prior order or direction of the Court of Appeal, (c) when a notice of appeal or an application for permission to appeal is not filed within the time limit, strike the appeal or application or extend the time to appeal or to seek permission to appeal, (d) dismiss an appeal if it has not been significantly advanced in over 6 months and significant prejudice has resulted to a party, (e) grant permission to intervene, and (f) refer any application to a panel of the Court of Appeal.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021); Alta.*

commentary.text:
In applications for leave to appeal under the , the affidavit should not contain evidence that is not part of the Municipal Government Act record of proceedings before the subdivision and development appeal board (“SDAB”), subject to two exceptions: (1) an applicant may file an affidavit to present facts that support an argument that the SDAB breached the rules of natural justice or was biased, since “any record the [SDAB] would produce regarding the hearing would probably not disclose such misconduct”; 165and (2) the applicant may file an affidavit to present facts to demonstrate why a question of law is important to the applicant or the wider community. Bergstrom v. Beaumont (Town), [2016] A.J. No. 744, 2016 ABCA 221 at para. 34 (Alta. C.A.); see also , [2015] A.J. No. 791, 2015 ABCA 243 at para. 6 (Alta. Rogers v. Edmonton (City) Police Service C.A.) regarding importance to the applicant.
Filing deadlines – Rule 14.40(2) provides that applications to single appeal judges must be filed and served at least 10 days before the application is scheduled to be heard. The Information Note to rule 14.40 further adds that all materials “should be filed simultaneously, unless the application must be filed first to preserve a time limit”. Information Note, r. 14.40.
Rule 13.3 and the accompanying Information Note reminds parties that when counting days “the date on which the event or activity occurs is not counted”. Deadlines that fall on weekends or dates on which the place for filing is closed should be considered alongside the Interpretation Act, which provides that if this happens, the filing can be done the next day. R.S.A. 2000, c. I-8, s. 22(1)-(2); note that these sections of the apply to the Interpretation Act Rules: see r. 1.8.
“Failure to meet the deadlines in rule 14.40(2) has various consequences.  Sobeys West Inc. v. Edmonton (City), [2015] A.J. No. 75, 2015 ABCA 32 at paras. 18-19 (Alta. C.A.). Rule 14.90(1)(a)(i) contains a presumption that no costs are available for a late step; the Registry or presiding judge may decline to set a matter down that has missed the deadline, depending on various considerations and scheduling matters; late filing by a respondent will not be allowed to prejudice an applicant (rule 1.5(4)); and extreme cases of missed deadlines can result in appeals or applications being struck”. Sobeys West Inc. v. Edmonton (City), [2015] A.J. No. 75, 2015 ABCA 32 at paras. 18-19 (Alta. C.A.).

(b) if there is no time for filing permission to appeal specified in any enactment or these rules, must be filed and served within the time for filing appeals set out in rule 14.8 . [Filing a notice of appeal]

data.title: Application to reconsider a previous decision
data.text:
An application to reconsider a previous decision of the Court of Appeal must be filed and served and must be returnable prior to the filing of, and prior to the deadline for filing, the applicant’s factum.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021); Alta.*

Reg. 41/2014, s. 4]
sentences: An application to reconsider a previous decision of the Court of Appeal must be filed and served and must be returnable prior to the filing of, and prior to the deadline for filing, the applicant’s factum. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021)
An applicant can apply to the Court of Appeal for leave to consider a binding precedential decision of the Court.
R. v. Melnyck, [2014] A.J. No. 1033, 2014 ABCA 313 at para. 1 (Alta. C.A.).
The Court has the ability to overrule precedents, but uses this power cautiously.
R. v. Melnyck, [2014] A.J. No. 1033, 2014 ABCA 313 at para. 2 (Alta. C.A.).

The court’s function on an application to reconsider is not to determine whether the prior case was wrongly decided, but whether the case should be reconsidered. JL Energy Transportation Inc. v. Alliance Pipeline Limited Partnership, [2024] A.J. No. 575, 2024 ABCA 175 at paras. 5-6 (Alta. C.A.)
, [2020] A.J. No. 95, 2020 Edmonton (City) Police Service v. Deluca ABCA 31 at para. 6 (Alta. C.A.)
, [2020] A.J. No. 708, 2020 ABCA 251 at para. 5 C. (A.) v. Alberta (Alta. C.A.)
, [2021] A.J. No. 868, 2021 ABCA 237 at para. 4 (Alta. C.A.)
Peters v. Atchooay Lawrence v. Alberta (Director of SafeRoads), [2023] A.J. No. 994, 2023 ABCA 271 at para. 14 (Alta. C.A.).
The criteria for reconsideration include whether the precedent:
(a) is recent or old
(b) has been disproved of or is contrary to the decisions of other courts of appeal
(c) contains some ‘simple, obvious, demonstrable flaw’
(d) was created by overlooking binding statute or authority
(e) created settled expectations
(f) was Reasons for Judgment Reserved or a Memorandum of Judgment.

R. v. , [2016] A.J. No. 539, 2016 ABCA Sobeys West Inc. v. Edmonton (City), [2015] A.J. No. 75, 2015 ABCA 32 at paras. 18-19 (Alta. C.A.). at para. 15 (Alta. C.A.), citing Angelillo, [2006] S.C.J. No. 55, 2006 SCC 55 at para. 12 (S.C.C.).

data.title: Application to restore an appeal
data.text:
An application to restore an appeal that has been struck, dismissed or deemed abandoned (a) must be filed and served as soon as reasonably possible, and (b) must be returnable no later than (i) for a standard appeal, 6 months after having been struck, dismissed or deemed abandoned, or (ii) for a fast track appeal, 3 months after having been struck, dismissed or deemed abandoned.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021); Alta.*

Reg. 41/2014, s. 4; Alta. Reg. 36/2020, s. 22 effective May 26, 2020 (Alta. Gaz. April 15, 2020)]
sentences: An application to restore an appeal that has been struck, dismissed or deemed abandoned
(a) must be filed and served as soon as reasonably possible, and
(b) must be returnable no later than
(i) for a standard appeal, 6 months after having been struck, dismissed or deemed abandoned, or
(ii) for a fast track appeal, 3 months after having been struck, dismissed or deemed abandoned. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021)
Alta. Reg. 36/2020, s. 22 effective May 26, 2020 (Alta. Gaz. April 15, 2020)]

Rule 14.47 obligates an appellant whose appeal has been struck, dismissed or deemed abandoned to file, serve, and make returnable a restoration application as soon as is reasonably possible and must be returnable within the time limitations set out in the rule.
Rule 14.47 is written in mandatory terms and must be complied with.
Coleman v. Coleman Wass v. , [2014] A.J. No. 1443, 2014 ABCA 452 at para. 21 (Alta. C.A.)
Wass, [2020] A.J. No. 521, 2020 ABCA 180 at para. 22 (Alta. C.A.).
An appeal which is not restored within this prescribed time period is deemed to be abandoned under rule 14.65(3).
If an appeal is abandoned, the party who filed the appeal may not take another step to advance it.
Coleman v. Coleman, [2014] A.J. No. 1443, 2014 ABCA 452 at para. 22 (Alta. C.A.)
see also Martinez v. Chaffın, [2018] A.J. No. 851, 2018 ABCA 244 at paras. 5-12 (Alta. C.A.).

The decision is discretionary, and once an appeal has been deemed abandoned the threshold to restore it is heightened. Rancher Construction Ltd. v. Scott Construction (Alberta) Ltd., [2020] A.J. No. 324, 2020 ABCA An applicant whose dilatory prosecution of an appeal has activated rule 14.65(3) — resulting in their appeal being deemed abandoned — “must present cogent reasons to justify restoration of the appeal” and must meet a rigorous standard.
Coleman v. Coleman, [2014] A.J. No. 1443, 2014 ABCA 452 at para. 33 (Alta. C.A.).

data.title: Stay pending appeal
data.text:
An application to stay proceedings or enforce- ment of a decision pending appeal may be made (a) to the judge who made that decision, or (b) to a single appeal judge, whether or not the application was made to the judge who made the decision, and whether or not that applica- tion was granted or dismissed.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021); Alta.*

Reg. 41/2014, s. 4]
sentences: An application to stay proceedings or enforce- ment of a decision pending appeal may be made
(a) to the judge who made that decision, or

(b) to a single appeal judge, whether or not the application was made to the judge who made the decision, and whether or not that applica- tion was granted or dismissed. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021)
info_notes: The preferred practice is to apply first to the judge who made the decision, but the rule does not preclude a direct application to a single appeal judge.

sentences: To obtain a stay pending appeal, the applicant must establish: 1. an arguable (serious) issue to be determined on appeal
2. the applicant would suffer irreparable harm if the stay is not granted

data.title: Time limits for oral argument
data.text:
Unless otherwise permitted, (a) subject to clause (b), oral argument on an application, including a reply, before a single appeal judge or a panel of the Court of Appeal may not exceed 15 minutes for each party to the application, (b) oral argument on an application for permission to appeal, including a reply, may not exceed 30 minutes for each party to the application, and (c) consolidated applications are to be treated as one application for the purpose of this rule.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021); Alta.*

Reg. 41/2014, s. 4]

data.title: Applications without oral argument
data.text:
A single appeal judge or a panel of the Court of Appeal may hear and decide applications without oral argument.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021); Alta.*

Reg. 41/2014, s. 4; Alta. Reg. 72/2022 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2022)]
sentences: A single appeal judge or a panel of the Court of Appeal may hear and decide applications without oral argument. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021)

data.title: Applications not heard within 3 months
data.text:
Subject to rule 14.44(2) [Application for permission to appeal], if an application is not heard within 3 months after the date the application is filed, the application is deemed to be abandoned unless a case management officer otherwise directs.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021); Alta.*

Reg. 41/2014, s. 4]
sentences: Subject to rule 14.44(2) [Application for permission to appeal], if an application is not heard within 3 months after the date the application is filed, the application is deemed to be abandoned unless a case management officer otherwise directs. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 14.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. May 31, 2021)

commentary.text: If an application is deemed abandoned by the operation of this rule, the applicant must appear before the case management officer and seek to have it reinstated.
